english: Scrap Storage Core

The heart of a StashNet storage network. Drive Bays and Terminals within 6 blocks connect to it. Lock it with a code to protect the network's Drive Bays and Terminals. Hit it with a hammer while carrying a Storage Core to upgrade it; the code stays.
Drive Bay
Holds up to 4 storage drives. Only accepts drives. Protected by its network Core's code. Hit it with a hammer while carrying a Reinforced Drive Bay to upgrade it; the drives stay inside.
Storage Terminal
Browse, search, deposit and withdraw everything stored on your network's drives.
Crafting Terminal
A workbench wired into your storage network. Same recipes and skills as a workbench, but it can use ingredients stored on the network's drives (place it within reach of a Storage Core).
Network Forge

A forge wired into your storage network. Works like a normal forge (ore still goes into its smelting slots), but recipes can use ingredients stored on the network's drives. Place it within reach of a Storage Core.
Network Chemistry Station
A chemistry station wired into your storage network. Same recipes as a normal one, but it can use ingredients stored on the network's drives. Place it within reach of a Storage Core.
Network Campfire
A campfire wired into your storage network. Same recipes as a normal one, but it can use ingredients stored on the network's drives. Place it within reach of a Storage Core.
Network Cement Mixer
A cement mixer wired into your storage network. Same recipes as a normal one, but it can use ingredients stored on the network's drives. Place it within reach of a Storage Core.
Fetching ingredients from storage... click Craft again.
48-Stack Drive

The smallest storage drive. Holds 48 stacks, about one wooden crate. Its contents stay on the drive, even when removed. Only readable inside a StashNet network. Shift-click it while a Storage Terminal is open to empty its contents into the network. The bar under the drive shows how full it is, and the number in the middle is the percent used.

192-Stack Drive

Holds 192 stacks, about four crates. Crafted from three empty 48-Stack Drives. Runs hotter than a 48-Stack Drive. Its contents stay on the drive, even when removed. Only readable inside a StashNet network. Shift-click it while a Storage Terminal is open to empty its contents into the network. The bar under the drive shows how full it is, and the number in the middle is the percent used.
576-Stack Drive

Holds 576 stacks, about twelve crates. Crafted from three empty 192-Stack Drives. Runs hotter still. Its contents stay on the drive, even when removed. Only readable inside a StashNet network. Shift-click it while a Storage Terminal is open to empty its contents into the network. The bar under the drive shows how full it is, and the number in the middle is the percent used.
1728-Stack Drive

Holds 1,728 stacks, about thirty-six crates. Crafted from three empty 576-Stack Drives. Runs hot. Its contents stay on the drive, even when removed. Only readable inside a StashNet network. Shift-click it while a Storage Terminal is open to empty its contents into the network. The bar under the drive shows how full it is, and the number in the middle is the percent used.
5184-Stack Drive

The densest storage drive. Holds 5,184 stacks, about a hundred crates. Crafted from three empty 1728-Stack Drives. Runs the hottest. Its contents stay on the drive, even when removed. Only readable inside a StashNet network. Shift-click it while a Storage Terminal is open to empty its contents into the network. The bar under the drive shows how full it is, and the number in the middle is the percent used.
Reinforced Drive Bay

Holds up to 8 storage drives and takes about as much punishment as concrete. Only accepts drives. Protected by its network Core's code. Hit it with a hammer while carrying an Armored Drive Bay to upgrade it; the drives stay inside.
Armored Drive Bay
Holds up to 12 storage drives and is about as tough as steel. Only accepts drives. Protected by its network Core's code. If it is destroyed, its drives drop in a loot bag.
Storage Core

A better network Core. Drive Bays and Terminals within 12 blocks connect to it, and its drives give off less heat. Lock it with a code to protect the network. Hit it with a hammer while carrying an Advanced Storage Core to upgrade it; the code stays.
Advanced Storage Core
The best network Core. Drive Bays and Terminals within 24 blocks connect to it, and its drives give off the least heat. Lock it with a code to protect the network.
